explode's count of debris objects still to make

Key N, Navigation Control. Prints "Switching to navigation panel", shows the $C000 bitmap, loads NAV.PAC as the picture ($1BEE) and NAV.TIL to $4000 ($26B1), loads the system's map ($2E7A), sets the full-screen window ($8810), copies the ship's sector ($071E/$071F) to the chart's cursor ($C6/$C7) and to the map's entry 0 ($5510/$5530), plots the course ($2880), counts in $0D07 the ships in slots 1-5 whose target is the player (slot 0) and greys the menu's HELM line by it ($26C0), then loops: date, time, the chart ($2669) and the menu ($25CA). COCKPIT leaves the loop by dropping its return address ($2634)

The Navigation Control menu: CHART, HELM, STATUS, QUERY, SCAN, COCKPIT (strings from $26F1; HELM is offered only when no ship is near, $0D07, and the chart's destination is set, $FC00 positive). The choice jumps to CHART $2787, HELM $2728, STATUS $2694, QUERY $2A69, SCAN $2619 or COCKPIT $2634
SCAN: moves the chart cursor with the keys or the stick ($A33F, $264D), naming its sector ($27D6) and redrawing the chart with the cursor's brackets ($0D2F), until Return, Space or fire ends it

COCKPIT: when the ship has moved ($C8), takes the new sector from $5510/$5530 and sets it up (enter_sector); then leaves navigation by dropping the menu's return address and going back to the cockpit ($2E71)
Moves the chart cursor ($C6, $C7) by X across and Y up (the chart's rows count from the bottom), unless that leaves the 32 by 32 chart: carry set then, and the cursor stays
Redraws the chart around the cursor: marks the cursor's sector ($3069 with 5, $2F9C), draws ($8638, $28DD, $8658), and moves the frame counter $5E on every other call

STATUS: the status page is in the base overlay, so this forgets the models, loads SEG1 over SEG0, runs its status page ($AB87 with X = $1D, Y = $AE, A = 7), then loads SEG0 back and reloads the models
Loads NAV.TIL, the navigation chart's tiles, to $4000
Colours the HELM line of the menu: $5C, or $78 when X is nonzero, written to 7 cells of two screen rows at $E1FD and $E225
"Switching to navigation panel"
Pointers to the six menu items' names
The menu items' names: CHART, HELM, STATUS, QUERY, SCAN, COCKPIT
One flag a menu item: 1 offered, 0 greyed out (HELM's, at $2723, is set by nav_menu)
HELM's enabled flag in nav_item_enabled, written by nav_menu

HELM, the autopilot: flies the course in $FC00/$FC20 a sector at a time from the ship's chart position ($5510/$5530). When the course runs out it prints "Ship has arrived at destination" ($2847) and returns. Each step: draws the move ($30D7), marks that the ship moved ($C8), moves the ship's position, lets the time pass ($290F), recomputes the rest of the course ($2880), and stops when ships are near after an encounter ($0D07, recolouring the menu) or when helm_step_time returns nonzero ($B4: fire or a key during the step or its encounter)

CHART: the cursor starts on the ship; the cursor keys or the stick move it ($A33F, move_cursor) and each move makes it the destination ($072C/$072D) and recomputes the course ($2880). Return, Space or fire leaves; with a course set it prints "Course laid in Nav computer" ($282B). $072C is $FF (no destination) from opening the chart until the cursor first moves

Prints "SC" and the cursor's sector coordinates on the chart's info line ($9F56), and below it "-message-" when the sector at the cursor is one of the 31 entries of the system map's list at $5510/$5530 whose message word at $55D1 is not $FF, or blanks otherwise
"Course laid in Nav computer", then "Ship has arrived at destination" at $2847, "SC" at $2867, "-message-" at $286C and a blank line at $2876

Works out the course from the ship's sector ($5510/$5530) to the destination ($072C/$072D) as a list of sectors: each step moves one sector along each axis that still differs, so diagonally until one coordinate matches; the X list goes to $FC00 and the Y list to $FC20, ended by $FF. No destination ($072C negative), no course
Marks each sector of the course on the chart: for each one visible ($3013) it plots ($8763) and changes the chart cell at $FA00 from $7D to 7

The time one HELM step takes: $29CA gives the hours (5 straight, 7 diagonal, doubled in slow sectors and with a damaged drive); the clock advances an hour at a time with the time and date redrawn and, until the trip is stopped, the chart ($2669); fire, or a key waiting, stops it ($AB, counted up each hour from then). When the day changes: damage repairs itself ($2A53), the daily lists $07AE-$07BB and $0783 are cleared and the random generator reseeded ($A2DC). Then the chances of the step: spoiled cargo ($2A15), the map's entries moved ($2D38), the message line (window 1) cleared, the counters $0832-$0834 cleared and an encounter ($2991). Returns $AB, nonzero to stop

Checks for an encounter in the step's sector ($2C1E with the hours); when one comes, prints "Under attack" (with ships near, $0D07) or "Space craft detected", plays effect 4 and waits 20 ticks of wait_ticks (about two seconds); fire during the wait, or a key waiting after it, sets $AB to stop the autopilot. With ships near, nav_helm stops anyway ($277A). Sets $0D04 to $FF first

The hours a HELM step costs: 5 for a straight step, 7 for a diagonal one (A nonzero); doubled when the sector's kind ($2F75, divided by 16) has bit 7 in sector_kind_flags, and doubled again when the player's $0409 has bit 2 (a damaged drive)
"Under attack", then "Space craft detected" at $2A00

Per HELM step, with A the step's hours: a random 0-100 ($A298, 101 outcomes) under A / 2, rounded down, and four times that when the sector has a map entry of type $64 (an ion storm, query_hazard_names), spoils cargo: the hold is searched from its last slot ($0777 - 1) down, and the first slot holding a kind that spoils (cargo_spoils negative) becomes kind $14
When $0740 is set, a new day clears random bits of the player's damage flags ($0409 ANDed with two random numbers ORed together)

QUERY: describes the sector under the chart cursor. Prints the system's name from the map ($5505) and the coordinates, then builds the rest in the text buffer at $FA00 ($9DEE appends): "FEATURES " with a name for each of the sector's map entries that is a real object ($2BC0), and the sector kind's text (sector_kind_texts, a disk text when its high byte is $C0-$CF); then "SHIPS " with, for the ship's own sector, the objects it met there ($0D04-$0D06 after a HELM trip) or the ships present in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is zero; "none" where a list is empty. Prints the buffer ($9AFA). Then it searches the sector's entries from the last one back and prints the message of the first whose message word's high byte ($55D1 + 2 * entry) is not $FF, and waits for a key
Ends a QUERY list: after names it takes off the last ", "; with none it appends "none"
Appends the name of map entry type A: types below $64 by the object type's name pointer ($0B12/$0B13), $64 and up from query_hazard_names ($2C12); then ", "
"none", then "FEATURES " ($2BF6), "SHIPS " ($2C00), two carriage returns ($2C07), ", " ($2C0A) and the line breaks at $2C0D
Two carriage returns, the separator after each QUERY section
Name pointers for map entry types from $64: type $64 is "Ion Storm" ($2C14)
The high byte of query_hazard_names' pointer for type $64

Rolls for an encounter after A hours of HELM travel: the chance grows with the hours and the system's danger level ($077C, both through $B451, less $495, $B5E0), kept in $96. Up to three ship types are drawn ($2C8C) into $0D04-$0D06 with their factions in $97-$99 (none: $FF); with at least one, $2CD2 decides whether they attack ($0D07). The BMI after the first draw reads the N of pick_ship's last load, the faction for a ship (never negative for the types the classes hold) or $FF for none. Returns the first type, negative for none
Sets the chance in $96, then picks a ship type as pick_ship does

A random number below 100 at or over the chance $96 gives no ship ($FF). Otherwise a second random number below 100 is spent across the system's five class weights ($077D-$0781, the last first) to choose a class, and one of the class's four entries in ship_class_types ($2D24) is picked: a random number from 0 to 15 under 4 picks that entry; otherwise a random number from 0 to the player's rank value ($0C79), halved, picks it, 3 at most, so a low rank gets the first entries and a higher one the third and fourth. Returns the type in A and its faction ($0C1E) in X

Decides whether the encounter attacks: if the second or third ship is hostile to the first ($387E returns $FE) they fight each other and leave the player alone; with $073D set, a random number below $56 also lets them pass; otherwise the first ship's attitude to the player ($387E with X=4): hostile ($FE) means an attack ($0D07 counts up), $FF or a neutral faction 0 attacks half the time (a negative random number)
Four object types for each of the five ship classes pick_ship chooses from: class 0 types 12 12 12 12, then 2 2 5 5, 7 8 7 8, 3 3 6 6, 1 1 4 4
Once a day of HELM travel: every map entry with a motion kind (flags at $5550, bits 0-2) is moved by its kind's routine, the address from map_motion_routines written into the JSR at $2D56
JSR whose operand move_map_objects rewrites to the entry's motion routine
Low byte of the JSR operand move_map_objects rewrites
High byte of the JSR operand move_map_objects rewrites
When a system map is loaded: puts each entry of motion kind 3 or 4 (the orbits) at its place for the date, through the JSR at $2D82 rewritten the same way
JSR rewritten by place_orbiting_objects to the orbit routine
Low byte of the JSR operand place_orbiting_objects rewrites
High byte of the JSR operand place_orbiting_objects rewrites
Motion kind 1: the entry moves a random step of -1, 0 or 1 across and down, staying on the 32 by 32 chart
Motion kind 2: an RTS, the entry stays where it is

Motion kind 3: places the entry on the 16-step orbit at $2E11 by the day count ($0724/2 plus the system's phase $5610). An entry whose picture ($5570) is $6C-$6F gets the picture for its quarter of the orbit ($2DD2)
Motion kind 4: places the entry on the 32-step orbit at $2E31 by the day count ($0724/4 plus $5611), then sets its picture like motion_small_orbit
The BPL that ends motion_large_orbit; its two bytes are also where motion kind 0 would read its routine in map_motion_routines
The BPL's offset byte, also the high byte motion kind 0 would read
The motion routine of each kind from 1: $2D89 wander, $2DB9 none, $2DBA small orbit, $2DEB large orbit
The 16 chart positions (x, y) of the small orbit, a circle of radius 3 around the centre of the chart (16,16)
The y coordinates of orbit_small's positions, read in pairs with the x at $2E11
The 32 chart positions (x, y) of the large orbit, a circle of radius 6 around the centre
The y coordinates of orbit_large's positions, read in pairs with the x at $2E31
Leaves navigation or a base screen for the cockpit: restores the picture and view ($1525), $A14C, and redraws the cockpit ($3102)

Loads the system map of system $071D: the file "Q" with the system's digit ($2EA0) to $5100. Copies the system's six encounter bytes ($5612: danger level and five class weights) to $077C-$0781 and places the orbiting objects ($2D60)
The system map's file name, "Q" and a digit load_system_map writes
The system digit of str_system_file, written by load_system_map
Puts cargo of kind A into the first empty hold slot from the top ($0767 negative), noting X, the price paid, in $076F. Carry set when the hold is full
Called from the base overlay (SEG1, $AF57): finds the first hold slot from the top holding cargo kind A ($0767 counted from slot $0777) and empties it ($FF); returns with Z set when none was found
Empties every hold slot ($0767-$076E set to $FF, $0777 slots)
Counts the hold slots in use: returns 0 for none, $FF for a full hold, otherwise the count
Prints the disk text $CF9C+A
Takes the word $60/$61 off the credits ($0728/$0729) if there are enough: carry set when paid, clear (and nothing taken) when not
Adds the word $60/$61 to the credits ($0728/$0729), stopping at $FFFF
Clears the view window, x 24-199 and y 40-183 ($8E17), and draws it in pattern 1 ($8F80, $901D)

The kind of the sector at X, Y on the loaded system map: the tile code in the 32 by 32 grid at $5100 (row 31-Y; the LDY's operand at $2F96 is rewritten), looked up in the tile set's table at $5000. The kind is a multiple of 16
LDY from the map grid; sector_kind writes the address of row 31-Y into its operand, and X picks the column
Low byte of sector_kind's rewritten LDY operand
High byte of sector_kind's rewritten LDY operand: the grid row's page

Puts the system map's entries into the chart window buffer at $FA00 around the cursor X, Y: each entry with a picture ($5570, a tile code) inside the window ($3013) replaces the cell ($8763 finds it) unless the cell's tile hides things (bit 3 of its attribute at $5000). An entry with a heading (flag bits 3-4, set by set_ship_heading) shows the tile for that heading, a quarter or half the heading value added as the tile's attribute bits 0-1 allow; a tile with attribute bit 2 animates by the frame counter's low bits unless the entry's flag bit 5 is set
Carry clear when the sector X, Y lies in the chart window around ($51, $53): under 6 columns and 5 rows away. Returns X and Y as offsets from the centre
Lists the system map entries (of the 32 at $5510/$5530) that lie in sector X, Y: their numbers go to $3061, the pointer to the list in $74/$75 and the count in Y
The entry numbers sector_entries finds, up to eight

Fills the chart window buffer ($FA00, 11 cells across by 9 down, filled from the end) with the map grid's tiles around X, Y: columns X-5 to X+5 and rows Y-4 to Y+4 (rows counted from the bottom). Cells off the chart get tile A, or, when A is $2C, the tiles $2C and $2D in a checkerboard
The operand of CPY #: fill_chart_window writes $20 here for rows on the chart and 0 for rows off it, so a row off the chart takes the off-chart tile at every column
The operand of CPY #: fill_chart_window writes the window's left column here (X-6), where each row stops
Sets the heading of map entry A from the step X, Y: right 0, up 8, left $10, down $18, written into bits 3-4 of its flags ($5550); no step, no change

Redraws the cockpit's instruments (from frame_update every seventh pass, and after keys that change them): $8810, the speed ($31B2), the hit points ($3240), the weapon ($329C), the attack lamp ($3129) and the threat lamps ($314D), then falls into draw_tac
Redraws the TAC display: the data page ($336F) when $7C is 0, the target's picture ($3501) otherwise
Clears the TAC display: pattern 1 ($8F80), then $B788 and $B839 in SEG0

Lights the lamp at screen cell $E2F1 (and its copy at $62F1) in colour $8A when something in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is not zero (a missile, or a ship that is no threat) has the player (slot 0) as its target; $C5 otherwise

Sets the three lamps at $E33B, $E363 and $E38B (with copies at $63xx): for each of up to three ships in slots 1-5 whose type's $0AEF is zero, a level of 1 for present, 2 with a target, 3 with the player as its target; each level picks a colour from threat_colours ($319F). A fourth and fifth such ship count in $89 and $8A, which no lamp shows
Colour for a threat lamp level X+1, 0-3, from threat_colours
The threat lamps' colours for levels 0-3: $BC $C5 $24 $8A

The speed readout. In Newtonian flight ($0D02) the shown speed is the ship's actual speed ($7C21, at most 99), also written to $0415; "CF" or "NF" (from $323A) is printed, a reversed mark when the drive is damaged ($0409 bit 2), then the number ($9F56); then the speed bar: $7C21's value (at most $42) fills the bar at x $18-$5A, row $21, in pattern 5 against pattern 1 ($8C23)
"CF" for cruise flight and "NF" for Newtonian, the speed readout's labels

The hit-points bar: a quarter of the player's hit points (bits 2-8 of $051D/$051E), plus one, at most $3C, drawn at x $4E, row $13, in pattern 4 against pattern 1, in pattern 7 (the warning colour) when under 15

The weapon readout at column $1E, row $1E. For the beam: a reversed mark when it is damaged ($0409 bit 1), the heat level ($0D00/2, at most 3) as one of four symbols, A or M for automatic or manual fire, then " -". For a missile: its symbol ($7C), the count left and a space. The cells under the first character ($E366, $E33E) get colour $5D, or $2A when a missile cannot be fired (none left, or reloading, $0836). The launcher's damage ($0409 bit 0) was meant to reverse the count and stop it too, but the AND #$01 at $32F2 tests what print_char left in A, $BC or 0, so it never does. Then the weapon's two-character name ($3363) and its colours at $E36B/$E343 ($3367) and $E36C/$E344 ($336B), each also written to the copy at $63xx
The first of the two characters naming each weapon (beam, then the three missile types), the second being the next character
The screen colours of each weapon's name, two tables of four ($3367 and $336B)
The second colour table of weapon_colours, written to $E36C/$E344

The TAC's data page. With no target, an empty name line, the hit points of the player ($345D) and the systems ($3480). For a ship target (slots 0-5): name ($33B5), its label ($33EA), the range ($33F8), its tactic ($3435), hit points and systems. Any other target: name and range. Ends in $87FE
Prints the target's type name ($0B12/$0B13) at column $0E, row $2E, padded with spaces to column $15; a reversed mark first when the target is a ship targeting the player
Prints the target's own three-character label ($366D) at column $15, then turns reverse off

Prints "RAN " and the range to the target: the distance from the player ($7947), a log, plus 2 (four times the distance) and made a number ($B5E0); $75 or more in the top byte prints "30+ km", otherwise the number ($9EBF) and "m"
Prints "TAC " and the ship's tactic ($043F), its name from the list of eight-byte names at $0CAE
Prints "ARM  " and the slot's hit points ($051D, $9EBF)
Prints "SYS " and six system letters, c f a e b m, for the bits $20 $10 $08 $04 $02 $01: a space for a system the ship's type does not have ($0C45), reversed for one damaged ($0409)
One letter of tac_systems: bit A of the type's systems ($0C45) and of the slot's damage ($0409) decide blank, reversed or plain; Y holds the letter

"30+ km", printed in place of the range when it is too great for the number ($75 or more in its top byte, tac_range); then the TAC labels "RAN " ($34EC), "TAC " ($34F1), "ARM  " ($34F6) and "SYS " ($34FC)
"RAN ", the TAC's label for the range, zero-ended; print_text's patched LDA at $9BAA still pointed here when the snapshot was taken

The TAC's picture page: the player's target (or the player's own ship with none) drawn in the TAC window in 3D. Clears the window (pattern 1, $B788, $8E17 at x $70, y 9, $4F by $2D), sets the drawing scale ($66CA with $0200), draws the model ($354C), then $B839, puts back the main view's flag $3A and scale ($66CA with 0) and ends in $87FE

Draws slot $A2's model in the TAC: the viewing distance is the type's $0A63 word plus $02CE (kept at $366A). The camera is the player's orientation (slot 0's block at $044B, or the identity at $0DA8 when the TAC shows the player's own ship) with its third row replaced by the way from the slot to the player ($92CC) and made orthonormal ($923E); that row times the distance ($95A0) is turned into the slot's frame by the slot's orientation (the identity past slot 6, $9160, $934B), and the two orientations are multiplied into $0D40 ($91B0). Then jumps into the model's own code through the type's model pointer ($08F8/$08F9) with the type's $0999 and $0A63 words in $76/$77 and $5F/$60
Nine bytes whose address tac_draw_model passes to the model's code in $74/$75, with $0D40 in $78/$79
The viewing distance tac_draw_model works out, three bytes
tac_distance's middle byte
tac_distance's top byte
Prints the three-character label of ship slot A, kept at $0421+3*A (each ship has one, from fill_slot)

The computer ships' minds, every 17th call (counter $3808, 16 down to -1): for each ship in slots 5-1 whose AI state ($041B) is not 0: works out the distance to its target ($7947, kept in $D0-$D4); every third time round (counter $3809), for a ship whose $0403 is clear, a ship without a target looks for one ($3701), one with a target reconsiders its attitude ($3739) and tactic ($375F). Every time, a ship with a target sets its speed ($37A8), steers ($3CAB) and may fire ($38C1). Then $3A2D

A ship without a target takes the one in $0439 if it has been given one; otherwise looks for an enemy ($3811). Found: it becomes the target ($0445), and $C6. None: AI state 1, tactic 0 (cruise) at that tactic's speed ($0C9A), and one time in eight $3CDC
Unless its AI state is 2, the ship decides how it stands to its target ($3BE0): AI state $FE to fight, or $FF with tactic 7 (flee)

For a ship that is fighting ($041B = $FE): beyond $0861 in distance (a log: about 333 units) the tactic is 2 (pursue). Otherwise a ship cruising or pursuing takes the type's own tactic ($0C38), and one in any other tactic changes, one time in ten (a random number of $E6 or more), to one of seven drawn from ai_tactic_choices. The distance test is signed: a negative log (very close) counts as near

Sets the ship's speed ($0415) from its tactic: the tactic's speed ($0C9A), or, against a ship target, by the tactic's speed rule ($0CA4): negative takes the target's speed ($7C21), 1 the average of the two, 2 one from the distance ($37E7), 0 leaves the tactic's speed

Speed rule 2: 5 when the target is more than about 45 degrees off the nose (negative $D4 or $D2/$D3 below $FF7D), otherwise $4B while far ($D0/$D1, a log, at $0861 or over: about 333 units) and the tactic's speed while close
Counts ship_ai's calls from 16 down; the minds run when it passes zero, on every 17th call
Counts ship_ai's passes 2, 1, 0: target, attitude and tactic are reconsidered at 0
The seven tactics ai_tactic draws from: close, follow, swerve, stand, circle, elude, ram

Looks among ship slots 0-5 (not itself, in use, $0403 clear) for the one its faction most dislikes ($387E most negative, $FE before $FF); if none, takes the target of a ship of a faction it is allied to (attitude 2). Returns the slot in Y, negative for none

How faction A stands to faction X: from the player (X = 4) it is the player's standing with that faction ($072E+A), except that a type-$0C ship (in Y) is unfriendly ($FF) while the player has a bounty ($0726/$0727), and otherwise takes the standing like any other ship (the LDA #0 at $3899 is overwritten by the next instruction); a negative faction gives 0. Between two computer factions it is faction_table entry A*4+X. $FE is hostile, $FF unfriendly, 0 neutral, 1 friendly, 2 allied
How each of the four factions stands to each other, row by faction: 1 FF FF FE / 0 1 1 FF / FF 2 2 FE / FE FE FE 2

A fighting or fleeing ship ($041B negative, $0403 clear) whose distance to its target is below $08A4 as a log (about 400 units, a beam's reach in trace_beam) fires three times in ten (a random number below $4D). The flag $BD is set when the value $7947 left in $D2-$D4 has a positive top byte and a low word at or above $FFCB as a signed comparison: the target within about 30 degrees of the nose. Then three times in ten a missile of its type's kind ($0C5F + 8; none with a damaged launcher, $0409 bit 0, or a type without missiles), a type 11 missile only with $BD set; otherwise the beam ($20EC), with $BD set or when its type's beam value ($0C52) has bit 7 set

Key G, surrender. Clears the view and shows the surrender text ($CF88). It counts only with exactly one ship fighting the player and the first time ($0832): then the rank count $072B gains $072A. A faction hostile to the player refuses ($CF81); one time in five any other ignores it ($CF7F). The Imperium (faction 2) asks for the bounty ($0726/$0727) plus 50 credits ($CF87, Y/N $3BA1): paid, the bounty is cleared ($CF86) and that ship and every computer ship's missile leave; too little money, $CF85. Any other faction asks for the cargo ($CF84): yes with an empty hold gives $CF83, otherwise the hold is emptied ($CF82) and the ship and the missiles leave. After either, print_wrapped is called again with what clear_tac left in A and X. Refusing gives $CF80

Checked after ship_ai: a badly damaged merchant offers its cargo. Only once per encounter ($0832), when the player's target is a ship of faction 1 targeting the player, with under a quarter of its type's hit points ($0AA9 word / 4), no other ship targeting it or the player. The chance is a random 0-100 ($A298, 101 outcomes) under $43, halved when the player has under a quarter of its own hit points and again when that faction is hostile to the player. Then the view shows the offer ($CF8D and a random cargo name, $2EF7 with 0-19, and "?") with AGREE or REFUSE ($3BA1): refused, $CF8C; agreed, $CF8B, and with room in the hold ($CF89 if full) one or two units of that cargo ($CF8A, cargo_add), every computer ship's missile and the ship leave, the standing with faction 1 may drop (one time in four), and $079A counts it when $079B is set
Shows the two-item menu AGREE / REFUSE ($99DE with the list of pointers at $3BCF) centred on the message window, then prints character $11. Returns Z set for AGREE
The closing quote and line breaks after an offer, then the pointers to "AGREE" and "REFUSE" ($3BD3) and the words themselves

Whether ship X fights target Y: a score from 4 less than A, plus the ship's hit points in eighths of its type's maximum, plus half the difference of the two types' rank values ($0C79), plus one when the factions are hostile, plus two when the target already has a given target ($0439), minus two when the ship has one, minus one for faction 1, plus two for faction 2, and exactly 2 for faction 3. Returns it in A: negative means flee. A target past slot 5 always gives 1
Changes the player's standing with faction Y by A, between -2 and 2; a negative faction or faction 3 is left alone

Steers a computer ship once it has stopped rotating: by its tactic's steering mode ($0C86): negative none, 3 random rates ($3CDC), 2 turn to the target's heading (its forward vector, $045D+27*slot, or $0DBA past slot 6), 0 turn toward the target, 1 turn away from it
Gives ship X random turn, pitch and roll rates, each -32 to 32 ($3D61)
A random rate from -32 to 32: the random byte's low six bits less $1F, less one more when random's carry is clear

Turns ship X toward the direction at ($74): rotates it into the ship's frame ($9160 with the ship's orientation), finds its two angles in 1024ths of a turn ($983B into $6F-$73), takes the tactic's offset (A, from $0C90) off the size of the first, so that the ship settles with the target that far to one side, and divides each angle by the type's turning step (its log less $0BE2's), clamped to a signed byte ($B447, $B5C5, $B771): the steps for the turn rate ($0516) and, its sign turned, the pitch rate ($0508)
Makes a ship's three-character label in $85-$87 ($3E1D each)
A random digit 0-9 or capital letter A-Z

The 3D view's draw list, from $A488 each frame: clears every slot's on-screen flag ($0621), tests every object in use against the view ($3EB8 with the type's radius from $0A63), keeping up to 14 in view; then draws them from the farthest to the nearest: each time the remaining entry with the greatest depth ($0D7E/$0D70) is drawn ($6400 with carry set, then $7033) and taken off the list
The operand of LDX #: build_draw_list writes the number of entries less one here, the index the search for the farthest entry starts from
build_draw_list's count of entries still to draw

Whether the object at ($58) relative to the viewer ($5A) is in the view: its distance along the view axis must be within its radius of the front ($94E7, $0D3E), and its sideways and vertical distances inside the view's slopes ($B398 with $0D6A-$0D6F and $0D68-$0D69). The three view coordinates go to $FF05-$FF0D + 9*entry. In view: depth to $0D7E/$0D70, the slot to $0D9A, on-screen flag $0621 set, and the size from $66AF to $0D8C; a far, small object (size under $0B) is drawn at once ($6400) and the carry comes back clear. Carry set when it is to be drawn later
The last 12 bytes of SR, zeros that nothing reads

Draws draw-list entry $0D3D (its slot from $0D9A to $5C, type to $5D). With the carry set and a slot below 7 (an object with an orientation): the position relative to the camera ($58) rotated into the object's frame ($92CC, $9160, $934B) into $0D5B, and the object's orientation times the camera's ($5A) into $0D40 ($91B0). Otherwise the plain linear difference into $0D5B and the orientation at $0DCC. Then ($74) = the entry's view coordinates at $FF05, ($76) = the type's draw-data word ($0999), $5F/$60 = its scale ($0A63), $4D = its screen size ($0D8C), and the type's draw routine ($08F8) is entered through ($94). A far, small 3D object (carry clear, type flag bit 7) is drawn as a dot instead ($8834 with $6518, half size); a type without flag bit 7 gets its colour pattern ($8F80) and its centre projected ($6773) first, unless it is behind the viewer
The colour byte for draw_object's far objects: $99, read by $8834 as its draw data

Moves the camera of the outside views, from the main loop: nothing in the cockpit ($0D3C = 0). Chase view (1): the camera at $668B is moved along $0896 by a step of sign(12 - d) * sqrt(|12 - d|) / 128, d its distance from the player (camera_offset). Cinematic view (2): once the ship is 100 or more away ($06A4 in log form) the camera is put back ahead of it (place_camera). Then both look at the ship: the offset becomes row 2 of the camera's orientation at $6694, $0DB1 (straight up) row 1, and mat_orthonormal finishes it

Sets up the view mode in $0D3C (from the V key, $6B22 and INIT): the cockpit puts the camera at the player's position ($065D) with the player's orientation ($044B) and stops the player's own ship being drawn ($0649 = 0); the outside views draw it and use the camera at $668B/$6694, placed ahead (place_camera). Prints the view's name (view_names)

Puts the outside camera ahead of the ship: the player's velocity ($0545) in log form, normalised, times 80 ($0652 in log form), back to linear, with 10 added to x's middle byte, plus the player's position ($065D), into $668B
The camera's offset from the player in log form ($668B less $065D, $92CC) into $6B-$73, and its length ($9531) in $5F/$60
Three pointers to the view names: cockpit, chase, cinematic
The high bytes of the view name pointers, read at $665F + 2 * view
"Cockpit view"
"Chase view"
"Cinematic view"
The outside views' camera position, 9 bytes (three linear 24-bit numbers)
x's middle byte of camera_pos, where place_camera adds 10
x's high byte of camera_pos, carried into by place_camera
The outside views' camera orientation, 27 bytes: three rows of three log-form numbers; row 2 at $66A6 points from the ship to the camera
An object's size on screen from its log depth in $5F/$60 (less the view's front $0D3E, from in_view): the antilog of $0D64 less it, $FF when that is 256 or more; returned in A

Sets up the projection from the log-form zoom in $5F/$60 (0 from INIT, the TAC's own from $3532/$3549), kept in $0D68: $0D64 = zoom plus log2 of the view's width $41, $0D66 = $0D64 less $31/256 (a slightly smaller vertical scale), $0D6A = $0D66 less log2 of the height $42; $0D6C and $0D6E = log2 of sqrt(1 + v*v) for $0D68 and $0D6A ($675C), the view's edges for in_view
log2 of sqrt(1 + v*v) for the log-form v in $5F/$60: the log doubled, 1 added ($B398 with 0), and halved

Projects the log-form point at ($74) to the screen: x and y each divided by twice z (their logs less z's plus one), scaled by $0D64 and $0D66; when either log is 13 or more both are pulled in by the excess so the larger lands at 8192, which keeps the direction for clipping. Back to linear ($B5C5): x plus the centre $56 into $51/$52, y plus $57 into $53/$54
Mid-instruction in MAIN. SR's $154B jumps here as WON's entry, after the ending has loaded WON over MAIN at $6800

The missiles' built-in model (types 9 and 10; type 10 recoloured by its draw data at $0A16): the prologue every model starts with, which puts its header's address ($681E) in $7A/$7B and jumps to draw_model

model_missile's header, 36 bytes copied to $9A-$BD: $9A set once its normals are made, then the counts (10 points, 2 reference points, 4 normals, 7 polygons, 10 axis vectors) and the pointers to its tables at $6842-$6929

model_missile's tables: point parents and axes, the axis vectors in log form, reference points, normals (filled in on first use), the polygons' order, normal and colours, their vertex counts and vertex lists
The player's Sunracer, type 0's built-in model: prologue with its header at $6935
model_sunracer's header: 19 points, 3 reference points, 8 normals, 10 polygons, 11 axis vectors, and the pointers to its tables at $6959-$6AB2
model_sunracer's tables, laid out as model_missile's

Tests every pair of objects for contact, once a pass from the main loop. For each ship slot 5..0 with a hit radius ($0635), against every slot 19..0 with one: the two types' radii ($0A1D words) are added and within_range ($74A3) checks the two positions box-wise against the sum; on contact on_contact ($6B22) handles the pair. Each ship slot's collision cooldown $040F counts down by one. $0837 starts each pass at $FF: on_contact sets it to the base the player touched
The ship's radius in $C8/$C9
($74) the ship's position, ($76) the other object's position; $60/$61 the sum of the radii
The ship's collision cooldown ($040F) counts down to zero

Slot $C6 (a ship) touches slot $C7. In an outside view ($0D3C nonzero) touching a base (type flag bit 0) just puts the view back in the cockpit (set_view). In the cockpit view, when one of the two is the player and the other's type has flag bit 7 (a 3D model) without bit 5 (not a missile), the other's slot goes in $0837 and nothing else happens here: dock_check ($7033) settles the touch when that object is drawn, so something out of view cannot be rammed. Every other pair goes to collide ($6B6C)

The collision proper between slot X and slot Y ($B2/$B3, their types in $B8/$B9; Y's type is also kept in $0835 as the last thing that hit). By the second object's type: type $1B blows up the first (hit_shard); a Malir gate ($14) touched by the player goes to gate_contact ($6C54); when either is a missile (flag bit 5) missile_hit ($6C7E); a hazard (flag bit 6) hazard_hit ($6CC5); anything else is a ram ($6BC3)

Type $1B (a hazard and a particle): it explodes and the first object takes its damage ($0AEF, 33) through blow_up ($6E4B); a new $1B is made at the origin ($0DC3), which place_particles ($7772) then moves near the camera

Two objects ram each other. Each ship's cooldown is checked (contact_cooldown, which leaves when it was already running); when the player is one of them the window flashes (set_colour with the code in $8C, fill_window) and sound 9 plays. The damage is the relative speed: the two velocities ($0545 blocks) subtracted (vec_sub_to_log), the difference's length (vec_length) times 8 (3 added to the log's whole part), back to a whole number (log_to_lin), of which only the low byte is kept in $B7. Each takes that damage from the other (damage, $6EA0), then the two bounce apart ($6D08)
X attacker, Y victim, A = 0 (shields count fully)
Bounce: $7A/$7B point at the difference vector at $BA

The player touches a Malir gate: the dot product (vec_dot) of the ship's third orientation row ($045D) with the unit z axis ($0DBA) must be at least 0.8 either way (its log above $FFAE), that is the ship must be lined up with the gate's axis, and the speed (speed_of) 20 or more; then the trip starts (gate_jump, $7134). Otherwise nothing happens

A missile is in the collision. The missile is made the first object ($B2, slots and types swapped when it was the second), its type kept in $0835. A missile does not hit the ship that launched it ($0433). Touching anything in slot 6 and up, or a ship other than the one it is aimed at ($0445), it just turns into an explosion (type $22 at its position, the missile freed); a missile with no target hits any ship. A hit explodes the missile against the ship with its type's damage ($0AEF: 100 for type 9, 250 for type 10, 75 for type 11, the plasma torpedo by its death text) through blow_up ($6E4B)

The second object is a hazard (flag bit 6: planets, the black hole, type $1A, which the death texts make a corrosive gas cloud, and the stars $1C and $1D). The player hears sound 11; the first object takes the hazard's damage ($0AEF; 255 for planets and the black hole) with no attacker (X = $FF) and A = $FF (no shield reduction). A gas cloud ($1A) touched is replaced by a new one at the origin

For a ship slot X (below 6): sets its collision cooldown $040F to 2 and, when it was already running, drops the caller's return address so the caller (ram) leaves at once. This keeps one contact from doing damage on every frame

Separates slot X and slot Y ($94/$95) after a ram: both are backed off one step along their velocities (back_off) and given a random turn (jolt_turn). When the second has flag bit 4 (it moves) the bounce is an elastic collision with the radii ($0A1D) as the masses: with d the relative velocity at ($7A) (first less second), the first's velocity becomes the second's plus d (r1-r2)/(r1+r2) and the second's becomes its own plus d 2r1/(r1+r2), the textbook head-on result. Against something that does not move, the first just reverses its velocity (reverse_velocity)
Velocity of slot Y = the second's velocity (at ($76)) plus the vector at ($7A) times the log-form ratio in $5F-$61 (vec_scale_signed, vec_log_to_lin, vec_add_lin)
Negates the velocity of slot Y (its $0545 block, vec_neg_lin)
Moves slot Y back one step: its position less its velocity (vec_sub_lin)
A computer ship (slot 1-5) gets a random turn rate ($0516) after a ram

Slot X (a missile or a type $1B hazard) explodes against slot Y, which takes damage A ($AA). When Y is the player the window flashes (code $12), the ship is jolted (jolt_player) and sound 5 plays, otherwise sound 6. An explosion (type $17) is made at X's position, Y takes the damage (damage, attacker X, with A = 1 when X is a type 11 missile so the shields count one step less), and X's slot is freed
Puts random numbers in the low bytes of the player's three velocity components ($0545, $0548, $054B): a small random jolt

Slot Y takes damage $80 from slot X (X = $FF for no attacker); A ($A0) is 0 normally, 1 for a type 11 missile (one step of the shields less), $FF for no shield reduction. Nothing for zero damage. A slot 6 and up is never damaged, but a base (type flag bit 0) hit by the player sets $0783, which the base code reads when you dock ($A5B1 in SEG1) and which is cleared when the day changes. A ship with $0403 set is simply freed. Otherwise the ship may remember its attacker in $0439 ($6EDC: the player, a missile's launcher, or a ship that was aiming at it, unless the attacker is in slot 6 and up or is already its target), the damage is cut by the shields (shield_reduce), and a computer ship is sent spinning (random_rates) when a random number from 0 to the damage comes out 6 or more. A hit of 10 or more knocks out a system one time in five ($6F4B) instead of reaching the armour; any other hit comes off the armour word ($051D/$051E), and below zero the ship is destroyed (destroy_object) with the credit going to the attacker (or a missile's launcher, $0433)

Records the attacker in $0439, the code above having left out an attacker in slot 6 and up or one that is already this ship's target: the player is recorded; a missile ($0403 set) whose launcher byte ($0433) is 0 or more records its launcher, whatever the missile was aimed at; any other ship is recorded only when it was aiming at this one ($0445)
A hit of 10 or more knocks out a system one time in five
The armour word of slot Y less the damage

Knocks out a random system ($6FC7; picked again when the first pick is the laser or the launcher): sets its bit in $0409, and for the player prints "<system> hit" on the message line ($9E4C, $9ADC) when the ship has that system ($0C45). The armour is spared; a system already out passes the damage on to the armour instead

The damage after the shields, in A. With A = $FF ($A0 negative) the damage stands. Otherwise bearing ($7947) gives the dot product of the victim's third orientation row with the line from attacker to victim; ROR $61 puts bit 0 of its sign in the carry, set for a hit from behind (the third row points to the ship's rear). A hit from behind uses the low nibble of the type's shield strengths ($0C6C), unless the aft shield is out ($0409 bit 3); from the front the high nibble, unless the fore shield is out (bit 4). Each step of strength halves the damage, one step less when $A0 is 1
A random system 0-5 in $A3 and its bit (1 shl $A3) in $A4: launcher, laser, engine, aft shield, fore shield, ECM
Pointers to the six "<system> hit" messages, indexed by the bit number of $0409
The high bytes of the system message pointers, read at $6FDA + 2 * bit
The messages, zero-ended: "Launcher hit", "Laser hit", "Engine hit", "Aft Shield hit", "Fore Shield hit", "ECM Unit hit"

Called by build_draw_list ($3EA6) after each object is drawn, for the object the player touched in the cockpit view ($0837 against the drawn slot in $5C), when its face signs are fresh. facing_face finds the first group of the model's faces all turned toward the player: none, and nothing happens; group 0 (a base's docking face) with a base (flag bit 0) and the player's speed (speed_of) under 21 docks (dock, dropping the caller's return); any other group is a collision (collide)

Walks the model's face groups (($BC) the size of each, ending with 0; ($BA) the normals they list): returns in Y the first group whose faces all have a negative sign in $FA36 (face_signs: turned toward the viewer), Z set for group 0; Y = $FF (N set) when there is none

Docks. In system 9 ($071D, the Manchi system) the game is won: load_won. Otherwise the models are reset, the screen cleared to colour 1 and bank 3 shown, the hum stopped ($1E = 0), SEG1 loaded over SEG0 and the base run (station_run, $A49A) until the player leaves. Then the slot models and SEG0 come back, the speed is set to 0, the ship is backed off twice along its velocity, its velocity made a unit vector away from the base (times 4 at a base whose map byte $5610 is $10), backed off once more, reversed, and given a collision cooldown of 8; the view goes back to the cockpit
The log of the speed the ship leaves a base with: $0000 (1) normally, $0200 (4) at a base whose map byte $5610 is $10
The whole part of the exit speed's log: 0 for speed 1, 2 for speed 4

The Malir gate trip. No base touched, no destination ($072C = $FF), speed $7F, the player's thrust doubled ($0C05 + 1), and 256 passes of flying with the particles streaming past (the flight routines without the keys). Then the current system's map is loaded and the gate in this sector found in it (type $14 at the sector $071E/$071F); its entry ($55B0) points to four bytes at $5630: the system, the sector across and down it leads to, and the number of rings to pass, kept in gate_dest. "Entering worm hole" ($CF1D) is printed, every slot but the player's freed, the ship turned to face along z at speed 5 and put at the origin with no velocity, the wormhole made (make_wormhole) and flown ($0838 = 1) until wormhole_rings says it is over. Enough rings passed: the system and sector become the gate's, the new map is loaded, "Entering " ($CF1B) and the system's name ($5505) printed; too few: "Faulty jump!" ($CF1C) and the old map reloaded. The sector is then entered ($0D04-$0D06 = $FF, the navigation tiles, an encounter roll of $10, enter_sector), and the thrust put back
256 frames of the jump: thrust, movement, then unless the frame is skipped (frame_skip3), the camera, the particles, drawing and showing the frame
Finds the Malir gate (type $14) in the current sector among the map's 32 entries
$CF1D printed, then everything but the player cleared away
The wormhole loop: thrust, turning, movement, drawing unless skipped (frame_skip5), the keys, wormhole_step and wormhole_rings, while it returns carry set
Rings passed against the number needed ($72C0)
Shows the buffer just drawn: bank 3 or bank 1 by $3A bit 7, and flips the drawing buffer (flip_draw_buffer)

Each wormhole frame: the ship moves a quarter unit along -z ($0663-$0665), and every 8th frame, unless $0741 is set, the armour word $051D/$051E loses one; below zero the player dies ($0835 = $1A, player_destroyed), with the corrosive-gas death text. Then the panel's speed and armour are redrawn
Where the gate leads, from the system map: the system, the sector across, the sector down, and the number of rings to pass
The sector across that the gate leads to
The sector down that the gate leads to
The rings of type $21 the gate needs passed for the jump to work

Carry set while the trip goes on. When the ship reaches the next ring position ($749C/$749D, every 14 units along -z): finds the rearmost and the foremost ring within 224 units; if the ship is not inside the rearmost (within_range with type $1F's radius, $0A5B) the trip is over (carry clear). Otherwise the rearmost is freed, counted when it is a type $21 ring, and unless enough are passed a new ring is made 14 units beyond the foremost, its x and y drifted by the bend (ring_drift)
A new bend: random length 0..19, half of it, random direction 0..7, from straight
The bend's amount grows by 2 a ring for the first half, then falls
Adds the bend amount ($74A0) to the new ring's x (Y = 1) or y (Y = 4) integer part, with the sign for the bend direction from drift_signs
The first eight rings, one every 14 units along -z from the origin, and the ring counters set: next ring position 14 units ahead of the ship, none passed
The type of ring number $749B: $1F for an odd number, $20 for 2 mod 4, $21 (the rings that count) for 0 mod 4
Signs of the drift for the eight bend directions, overlapped: y signs from $7491 (0, 1, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1, -1), x signs from $7493 (1, 1, 0, -1, -1, -1, 0, 1)
The x signs of the drift for the eight bend directions (1, 1, 0, -1, -1, -1, 0, 1), overlapping the y signs two bytes on
Rings made in this bend sequence; $749C/$749D the next ring position; $749E/$749F the bend's length and half; $74A0 the bend amount; $74A1 the bend direction; $74A2 the rings passed
Low byte of the next ring position along -z, moved 14 units on for each ring
High byte of the next ring position along -z
Rings left in the current bend, counted down; below zero a new bend starts with a random length of 0 to 19
Rings left in the bend's first half, while its amount grows by 2 a ring; after that it falls by 2
The bend amount, added to each new ring's x and y with the direction's signs
The bend direction, 0 to 7, an index into the drift signs
Rings of type $21 passed in this trip, compared with the gate's count at $72C0

Carry set when the positions at ($74) and ($76) are within the distance in $60/$61 on every axis, clear as soon as one axis is not: the integer parts of z, y and x (bytes 7-8, 4-5, 1-2) compared one by one, a box rather than a sphere. Used for collisions and the wormhole's rings

Speeds up or slows every ship toward its set speed: computer ships 5..1 always in cruise (cruise_thrust); the player in cruise when $0D02 is 0. In Newtonian flight ($0D02 set) the player's velocity changes only while the speed keys are held ($0D01 the direction): the type's thrust ($0C04, a quarter with the engine out) along the ship's axis is added, unless the new speed would pass the limit (a length of about 4.4 units a frame, 70 in the game's speed units)

Cruise flight for ship X: the wanted velocity is minus the third orientation row times the set speed ($0415) / 16; the velocity moves toward it by at most the type's thrust ($0C04 log word, a quarter with the engine out) each frame, or takes it when closer than that
The third orientation row of ship $94 times the log-form number in $5F-$61, as a linear vector at $0896
Divides the log-form number in $5F/$60 by 4 when ship $94's engine is out ($0409 bit 2)
Adds each moving object's velocity ($0545 block) to its position ($065D block): every slot 19..0 in use whose type has flag bit 4

Turns the ships and the planet: slots 6..1 with a pitch, turn or roll rate are turned by turn_ship (slot 6, the planet, has its turn rate stepped up each frame so it keeps spinning). Then the player's three rates ($050F roll, $0516 turn, $0508 pitch, in 1024ths of a turn) become radians and turn the player's orientation ($044B, turn_by_rates), and the camera's orientation is transposed into $0DCC for drawing
The signed byte in A, an angle in 1024ths of a turn, to log-form radians: int16_to_log, less $0759 (log2 of 1024 / 2 pi)

Turns computer ship X: its type's turning step ($0BE2, a log word in 1024ths of a turn) is used on each axis whose rate is nonzero, with the rate's sign, and the rate counted one step toward zero; the angles turn the ship's orientation ($044B block, turn_by_rates)

Re-places the space particles (types with flag bit 2) in slots 19..6 that are off screen or too close: their on-screen value $0621 (set by build_draw_list) 0 or 7 and more. They go around a point ahead of the camera (place_particle), so the particles always stream past the viewer

A particle in slot Y: a moving one (flag bit 4) has its velocity cleared ($0DC3). The first one this frame works out the centre: a point 37 units ahead of the camera ($7838), pushed 21 units further along the way that point has moved since last time ($7872); every particle then goes to the centre plus a random offset of up to 10 (random_offset)
The point 37 units ahead of the camera ($011D): the camera's position ($58) plus its third orientation row ($5A + 18) times -37 (log $0533, sign $FF)
The point ahead of the camera from the last time particles were placed (9 bytes, a linear position)

Gravity. For each object in slots 19..6 whose type has flag bit 1 (planets, the black hole and the stars $1C and $1D), each ship slot 5..0 with a radius is pulled toward it (gravity_pull) and the pull added to its velocity. The strength is from the type's $0A63 log word, less 2, doubled

The pull of object ($74) on ship ($76) at $6B: the unit vector toward the object times the strength over the distance squared (log: $96/$97 less twice the log of the distance), so it falls with the square of the distance. When the pull on the player reaches 2^-9 (log $F700) "Warning: nearing strong gravity well" ($CF1E) is printed, once ($0834, cleared each HELM step)

For slot X and slot Y: the vector from X to Y in log form at $0896, its length in log form in $80/$81 (also $5F/$60), made a unit vector, and its dot product with Y's third orientation row ($045D block) in $5F-$61. Y is saved into the operand at $797D for that last step
The LDY operand at $797D is the slot saved at $7947
The slot bearing saves at $7947, the LDY operand that picks Y's orientation for the dot product

The four arrowheads that point to the player's target ($0445). The target's position relative to the player, turned into the ship's frame (mat_times_vec with $044B) and projected; each screen coordinate held to the window, counting how many were inside. When the target is ahead (its z sign in $08A7 negative) and on screen, the arrowheads sit on the four edges pointing in at its x and y; otherwise they are drawn 5 pixels (3 rows) in and point outward, toward where it lies
An arrowhead 9 rows high at x $47, row $53 (the target's y) as its middle: one pixel wide at the top widening to 5 and back, pointing right
The same arrowhead pointing left, ending at x $47
An arrowhead at the target's x ($51, even) and row $4B: 8 pixels wide narrowing over 4 rows upward
The same arrowhead pointing down from row $4B
The speed of slot Y, a whole number in A: its velocity's length times 16 (4 added to the log's whole part), back from log form. Docking wants under 21, a Malir gate 20 or more
Points ($74) at slot Y's position: $065D plus 9 * Y ($0846)

Every 3D model's code starts by putting its 36-byte header's address in $7A/$7B and jumping here, with ($74) its position relative to the camera (log form), ($78) its orientation, ($76) an optional colour table and $5F/$60 its scale. The header is copied to $9A-$BD; the first time ($9A = 0) the model is prepared (prepare_model). Then the points are placed (place_points), the faces tested (face_signs) and the polygons drawn (draw_polygons)

A model's first use: each axis vector's log has the scale in $5F/$60 less $06A4 (100) added, unless the component is near zero (whole part below -10); the points are worked out in the model's own frame (place_points with the identity at $0DA8 and the zero vector at $0DAB); the reference points ($A0) are stored, linear and negated, in the table at ($A8); and each normal ($AA) is made as the cross product of two edges of its polygon, from the vertex list ($B6, the counts at $B8)

Places the model's points: each axis vector ($A4, $9F of them) is turned by the orientation ($96, vec_times_rows) into $FA52; then each point ($9B of them) is its parent (the position ($98) for a negative entry in ($A6), else an earlier point) plus or minus an axis vector (($A2), negative to subtract), into $FB00 + 9 * n; a point in front of the viewer (z negative) is projected ($6773) and its screen x and y kept at $FC20 + 4 * n

For each reference point ($9C), its offset from the viewer ($0D5B) in log form into $FA00; for each normal ($9D), the sign of its dot product with its reference point's offset (($AC) says which) into $FA36: negative when that face is turned toward the viewer

Draws the model's polygons ($9E) in three passes for a painter's order: first those on the far side of the plane that ($AE) names for them (by its normal's sign in $FA36, a negative entry reversing the test), then those with 0 in ($AE), then the near ones (draw_polygon)

Draws polygon Y: the colour from ($B4) when its normal ($B0) faces the viewer, else from ($B2), $FF meaning not drawn from that side ($8F80 sets the pattern); its vertex count from ($B8) and its vertex list found by summing the counts before it in ($B6). Then on to clip_polygon
Points ($74) at model point A: $FB00 plus 9 * A

Copies the polygon's vertex numbers to $FD40 and clips it to the wedge in front of the viewer: none in front, it is dropped; all in front, it goes straight to fill; else clip_edges runs twice (the planes y = -4z and y = 4z, $86 = $FF then 0), new points made from $1C on are projected, and the screen coordinates of the vertices go to $FD00 (4 bytes each) for fill_polygon ($8288)

Walks the polygon's vertices at $FD40 testing each against one plane (plane_side): an edge crossing it gets a new vertex at the crossing (new_vertex), vertices inside are kept; the survivors go back to $FD40. None left: the polygon is dropped (the return address pulled)
The crossing of the edge from point X to point Y with the plane, by intersect_far or intersect_near ($86), written as a new point at $85 (from $1C up) and added to the vertex list at $FD50

Counts the polygon's vertices with z negative (in front) from $FB08: none, the polygon is dropped (the caller's return address pulled); all of them, clipping is skipped (on to $80B6); otherwise clipping goes ahead
Copies each vertex's screen coordinates from $FC20 to $FD00 in order and fills the polygon ($8288)

Which side of a clipping plane vertex Y of $FD40 is on, in $83 (1 inside, 0 outside): y's log against z's plus 2 (four times z), with the signs; $86 negative tests y <= -4z, else y >= 4z, the two together keeping only the wedge in front of the viewer. The final test is the BPL or BMI patched in at $8146
The BPL here becomes BMI (opcode $30) for the other plane: plane_side writes $10 or $30 into it
The crossing with the plane y = -4z: intersect_core with $68-$6A = $0200, sign $FF, then the new point's z sign inverted
The crossing with the plane y = 4z: intersect_core with $68-$6A = $0200, sign 0

Where the edge from ($74) to ($76) meets the plane: the edge vector ($96DE into $6B-$73, its signs flipped), the fraction along it from the ends' distances to the plane ($B35B), x and y of the crossing ($B392), and z set to y / 4 (y's log less $0200)

Fills the polygon of $55 vertices (2 to 8) whose screen coordinates are at $FD00 (x and y, 16 bits each): when all of them are inside the window ($43 wide, $44 high) it goes straight to scan_fill; otherwise it is clipped to y 0 to $42 and x 0 to $41 (clip_side four times) first

Clips the polygon at $FD00 against one side of the window: A is the branch opcode (BMI or BPL) patched into $8320 and $8343 to say which side is inside, X the limit and Y the coordinate given to new vertices, $81 0 for x or 2 for y. Vertices inside are kept and each edge that crosses the side adds a vertex on it (clip_point), into $FD80 and back to $FD00; with none left the polygon is dropped

Where the edge from vertex X to vertex Y crosses the window side: on an x side ($81 = 0) x is the side's value and y is interpolated, y1 + (y2 - y1) * (x - x1) / (x2 - x1), with logs ($B447, $B5C5); on a y side the other way round. Appended to $FD80
Copies vertex 0 after the last (at X) so the edge walk can close the polygon

Fills the polygon at $FD00 row by row: from the lowest vertex (the greatest y, rows counting up from the bottom) it walks the edges on the two sides (left_edge, right_edge), stepping x by the slope with an error term and INX or DEX patched into $854C and $855D, and draws each row's span ($8C9C) until the two sides meet

Starts the next edge on one side of scan_fill: the previous vertex, the edge's height in $83 and width in $82, and INX or DEX ($E8/$CA) patched in at $854C for its direction; edges of no height are skipped, and running out of vertices ends the fill
